lesson-philippine-constitution-bill-of-r.note: Traps to Watch For now follows Examples; Speed Tricks is optional.

lesson-philippine-constitution-bill-of-r.quote: A **bill of attainder** is a law that punishes a named or clearly identified person or group without a judicial trial.
lesson-philippine-constitution-bill-of-r.note: All five originally listed missing terms now have local glosses; a different new terminology gap is flagged separately.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: A person cannot be jailed just for supporting an unpopular political idea.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: Political-belief-only detention and its separate-crime limit are taught and applied.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: It allows an exception when the service is punishment for a crime after due conviction.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: Forced service is defined and the conviction exception is applied.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: Republic Act No. $9346$ prohibits imposing the death penalty.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: Excessive fines, other prisoner protections and current replacement penalty rules are now included.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: A lawful conviction does not give officials permission to abuse a prisoner.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: Cruel and degrading punishment, subhuman facilities and current statutory penalty rules are covered.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: A conviction or acquittal under either one bars another prosecution under the other for that same act.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: General same-offense prerequisites and the special national-law/local-ordinance condition are taught with examples.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: It may make an earlier lawful act a crime or increase the punishment after an offense was committed.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: Meaning and two different harmful backward penal applications are supplied.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: The legislature imposes punishment itself instead of leaving guilt and punishment to a court.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: Meaning and legislative group punishment application are supplied.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: Use available evidence, such as records, witness accounts, or medical findings.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: The analysis method requires facts, rights, conditions and evidence; Example #12 applies it.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: Unlawful detention may stop a person from working or caring for family.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: Social effects are explained and Example #13 connects liberty loss to family income.

general-information-philippine-constitut.quote: A person may seek a lawyer or legal aid and ask a court for the proper remedy.
general-information-philippine-constitut.note: Counsel, court remedy, habeas corpus and CHR powers are described; Example #14 applies remedy selection.

lesson-philippine-constitution-bill-of-r.quote: Filing a complaint alone does not meet these conditions.
lesson-philippine-constitution-bill-of-r.note: Double jeopardy now has meaning, attachment conditions, termination conditions and worked applications.
